subject: general
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

I felt nervous all through the interview, but I replied **as well as was possible** for anyone in the situation.

options.text: To the best of one's ability

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To the best of one's ability"** means doing something as well as one can, given the circumstances. (अपनी पूरी क्षमता से)

 
 
• **Example: **She completed the project** to the best of her ability** despite the tight deadline.
 
 
 
• **"To the best of one's ability"** signifies putting in maximum effort and doing the best one can under given conditions. (अपनी पूरी क्षमता से)
 
 
• **Example: **Even though he was tired, he played the game** to the best of his ability.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Run out of steam** (थक जाना): To lose energy, enthusiasm, or interest.

 
 
• **Example:** She started the marathon full of energy but ran out of steam halfway through.
 
 
 
• **Through thick and thin** (हर परिस्थिति में): To stay with someone or something through good times and bad.
 
 
• **Example:** True friends stick together through thick and thin.
 
 
 
• **Eats like a bird** (बहुत कम खाना): To eat very little.
 
 
• **Example:** She eats like a bird, which is why she stays so slim.
